title: Boron for Hair: What the Research Actually Shows
seo_title: Boron for Hair: Benefits, Evidence & Safe Intake | FullyVital
seo_description: Does boron help hair growth? What the research shows about boron, hormones and DHT, the best food sources, and how much is safe.
notes: Citation style v2 (your rule): 3 studies, each cited once, all in the second half; Key Takeaways and FAQ carry no links. Dropped Khaliq, Adil & Godwin, Ferrando, Nielsen, Hadrup and Naghii & Samman. Removed the DHT-drives-pattern-loss caution, the calcium/magnesium section, the boric-acid toxicity detail and the kidney explanation (general 'talk to your doctor' kept).
Removed claims with no evidence: that boron 'reduces hair loss', 'promotes regrowth', 'combats dandruff', 'balances sebum' and 'strengthens follicles'. No human study has tested boron on hair.
Added the DHT finding (Naghii 2011): boron raised DHT in men. Relevant and a caution for readers with pattern hair loss.
Removed the sections promoting boron-enriched shampoos, topical boron and DIY boron treatments; replaced with a boric-acid toxicity caution.
Corrected the dosage section: the old text called 3-20 mg/day generally safe; 20 mg is the upper limit, and typical intake is about 1 mg/day.
Food sources now follow the US diet analysis (Rainey 1999) instead of an unsourced list.

Replaced the old 'Sources' list. It cited a study about lithium (not boron), two Google Books search links and a supplement self-help book, with no links to studies. Every source is now a PubMed-verified study linked where it's used.
Added Key Takeaways, an FAQ answering the queries the page ranks for, and a reference list.
No reviewer or 'medically reviewed' line, as agreed.
